title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Glassy but waiting on the Fed swell
conditions.summary: Futures are inching higher after Monday's chip-led rally, as the Fed starts a two-day meeting and a big earnings day gets going. Oil above $100 and a 10-year yield near 5% keep a lid on things.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 0.1% and Dow futures about 0.2% as of roughly 5:30 AM ET; early quotes are thin.
Monday's close: S&P 500 +0.7%, Nasdaq Composite +0.8%, Dow +0.3%, with the Philadelphia chip index up 2.8% after Anthropic's IPO filing.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.99%, and the dollar index is up about 0.3% to 102.1.
WTI crude is near $102 a barrel and Brent near $111 to $116 depending on source, near six-month highs on Middle East supply fears; gold is down about 0.6% near $4,014.
Bitcoin is just under $80,000, down about 0.1% in 24 hours; the VIX sits near 18.3.
Asia was mixed: Japan's Nikkei rose about 1.7% and Korea's Kospi jumped, while Shanghai fell 1.3% and Hong Kong slipped 0.7%.
Europe is lower: the Stoxx 600 is down about 0.4% and the FTSE 100 about 1% as HSBC sank more than 6% on its results.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: The Fed begins its two-day meeting today; markets expect rates held on Wednesday after last month's hike, with focus on any hints of another hike.
7:30 AM CT: Durable goods orders for September, consensus +1.8%; ex-transportation +0.6%.
8:00 AM CT: S&P Case-Shiller 20-city home prices, consensus +2.7% year over year; FHFA house prices, consensus +0.1%.
9:00 AM CT: Conference Board consumer confidence, consensus 80.5 vs 81.9 prior; new home sales, consensus 649,000; Richmond Fed manufacturing, consensus 1.
Noon CT: 5-year Treasury note auction.
Backdrop: oil above $100 tied to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran keeps inflation worries alive, and US midterm elections are one week away.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Celestica beat after Monday's close: Q3 revenue rose 83% to $5.83 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.30 topped $2.96; shares up about 17% pre-market.
Whirlpool reported a Q3 loss and missed revenue estimates; shares fell nearly 9% after hours.
Before the open today: Boeing (expected loss of 21 cents a share; free cash flow in focus), Coca-Cola, Corning, PayPal (consensus EPS $1.31) and SoFi (consensus EPS 17 cents).
After the close today: Visa, Seagate Technology and Robinhood.
Later this week: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon headline Big Tech earnings.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: CLS (Celestica): +17% — Q3 revenue and profit beat on AI data center demand.
WHR (Whirlpool): -9% — Q3 loss and revenue miss.
SKHY (SK Hynix): +3% — report it may pay a special dividend of about $12 billion ahead of Wednesday's results.
AVGO (Broadcom): +1.4% — $63 billion financing deal with a Wall Street group to supply hardware to Anthropic.
CRWV (CoreWeave): +1.3% — bouncing after hitting a 52-week low Monday on neocloud worries.
TSLA (Tesla): +1% — extending Monday's 5% jump.
META (Meta Platforms): about flat — raised a record $97.5 billion in equity for AI, with Nvidia investing $3 billion.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO filing shows first-half revenue of $1.16 billion, up about 1,300%, with a listing possibly as soon as next month at a reported $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation.
Meta's record $97.5 billion equity raise includes a $3 billion Nvidia investment and an expanded AI partnership.
SpaceX closed $40 billion in GPU lease financing; Elon Musk ruled out buying neocloud companies.
HSBC fell more than 6% as wealth management slowed and costs rose, dragging European banks.
Brazilian stocks fell after President Lula's surprise re-election, and Israel holds national elections today.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT durable goods and Boeing's pre-market report set the opening tone.
9:00 AM CT consumer confidence and new home sales, then the noon CT 5-year auction with the 10-year yield near 5%.
After the close: Visa, Seagate and Robinhood, ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, October twenty seventh, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, sporting his Fed day bandana. Gus, give the crew a howdy! [BARK]

On this Dawn Patrol, conditions are fair, and pretty glassy. Stock futures are up about a tenth of a percent for the S and P five hundred and the Nasdaq one hundred, and about two tenths for the Dow. Those early quotes are thin. Monday was a fun session. The S and P rose seven tenths of a percent and chip stocks surfed nearly three percent higher after Anthropic filed for its I P O. The ten year Treasury yield sits near four point nine nine percent. Oil is around one hundred two dollars a barrel, gold slipped about six tenths of a percent, and bitcoin is just under eighty thousand dollars. Over in Asia, Japan rose almost two percent. Europe is lower, as H S B C wiped out more than six percent on its results.

Now the wind and weather. The Fed starts a two day meeting today. Markets expect no change on Wednesday, after last month's hike. Durable goods orders land at seven thirty A M Central, with forecasts near one point eight percent. Consumer confidence and new home sales follow at nine A M Central.

On the tide chart, Celestica crushed it, with revenue up eighty three percent. The stock is up about seventeen percent before the bell. Cowabunga, that's a wave! That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK] Whirlpool had a gnarly wipeout, down nearly nine percent on a loss. Before the open we hear from Boeing, Coca-Cola, Corning, PayPal and SoFi. After the close, it's Visa, Seagate and Robinhood.

In the lineup, S K Hynix is up about three percent on talk of a twelve billion dollar special dividend. Broadcom is up more than one percent on a sixty three billion dollar financing deal to supply Anthropic. CoreWeave is bouncing, and Meta is flat after a record ninety seven and a half billion dollar stock sale, with Nvidia chipping in three billion.

Sets to watch: durable goods at seven thirty, consumer confidence at nine, and the five year note auction at noon Central. Stay loose, the real swell arrives with the Fed on Wednesday and Big Tech later this week.
